titleEn: The Economist — Interview with Elon Musk
summaryEn: A wide-ranging interview with Elon Musk conducted by The Economist.
summaryZh: 《经济学人》对埃隆·马斯克进行的一次内容广泛的访谈。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk, thank you so much for joining me on the Insider. Thank you for having us. Here at Tesla Giga, it is really hard to introduce you without using superlatives. I mean, you are doing, I think, more to build the future than literally anybody alive right now.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克，非常感谢你做客《Insider》。谢谢你邀请我们。在这座Tesla超级工厂里，介绍你时真的很难不用最高级的词。我是说，我认为，在建设未来这件事上，你所做的事情确实比目前任何一个在世的人都多。

segments.textEn: I'm doing a lot of building in general.
segments.textZh: 总的来说，我确实在做很多建造工作。

segments.textEn: You're doing a lot of building?
segments.textZh: 你确实在做很多建造工作？

segments.textEn: Instinctive builder, I suppose. I just like building things.
segments.textZh: 我想，我是个凭本能行事的建造者。我就是喜欢建造东西。

segments.textEn: You are, but you're building, I mean,
segments.textZh: 你确实是，但你正在建造，我是说，

segments.textEn: you, you know, run around building things all day long.
segments.textZh: 你，你知道，整天到处跑着建造东西。

segments.textEn: You run around building a lot of things. You pioneered electric vehicles, you revolutionized space travel. You've got a cutting edge AI model now, humanoid robots. Can we start this conversation by you putting all of this together? Tell me what the world's going to be like in, let's say, 10 years if you succeed.
segments.textZh: 你到处跑着建造了很多东西。你开创了电动汽车的先河，你革新了太空旅行。你现在拥有一个尖端的AI模型，还有人形机器人。我们能否请你先把这一切串联起来，以此开始这场对话？告诉我，假设你成功了，比如说10年后，世界会是什么样子。

segments.textEn: 10 years. So we're talking 2036.
segments.textZh: 10年后。所以我们说的是2036年。

segments.textEn: Yep. Hopefully we'll both be around.
segments.textZh: 对。希望我们俩那时都还在。

segments.textEn: Hopefully, yes, we can, we can. Probably most likely we will be. It's hard to imagine the future that where there's not an overwhelming amount of artificial intelligence. Meaning like in 10 years I would expect artificial intelligence to be far greater than the sum of human intelligence. Like far greater. In fact, I think AI may exceed the sum of human intelligence in around five years. In five years, Roughly five years is my guess. So there really won't be anything that AI can't do better than humans, apart from being human, perhaps at a more
segments.textZh: 希望如此，是的，我们可以，我们可以。很可能我们都会在。很难想象这样一种未来，其中没有数量压倒性的人工智能。意思是，比如说，10年后，我预计人工智能将远远超过人类智能的总和。是远远超过。事实上，我认为AI可能会在大约5年后超过人类智能的总和。5年后，我猜大约是5年。所以，除了作为人类之外，真的不会再有任何事情是AI无法做得比人类更好的，或许在一个更

segments.textEn: prosaic level, what will life be like?
segments.textZh: 平实的层面上，生活会是什么样子？

segments.textEn: The most likely outcome is an age of amazing abundance where anyone can have anything they can think of. This may sound preposterous, but, well, here we are in 2026. Let's see where we stand in 2036. Now, of course there are things that could derail this, like a massive global thermonuclear war or something like that. But assuming that there's not World War 3, I think we're headed for an age of amazing abundance. So this is, I guess, a message of optimism and excitement about the future.
segments.textZh: 最可能的结果是一个惊人富足的时代，每个人都能拥有他们能想到的任何东西。这听起来可能很荒谬，但是，嗯，我们现在已经到了2026年。让我们看看2036年时会处于什么境地。当然，有些事情可能会让这一切脱轨，比如一场大规模的全球热核战争，或者类似的事情。但假设不会发生第3次世界大战，我认为我们正走向一个惊人富足的时代。所以我想，这是一个关于未来的乐观而令人振奋的信息。

segments.textEn: So we'll talk about the abundance in a second. But just on a very prosaic matter, how are your companies going to be making money? Because when you in the SpaceX IPO prospectus, it, it looked as though the overwhelming amount of the revenue would be coming from AI, from Grok, really, it won't be transporting things to space as Space X is now doing. What is, what will your companies be doing in 10 years and how will they make money?
segments.textZh: 所以我们马上会谈到这种富足。但只说一个非常实际的问题，你的公司要如何赚钱？因为当你在SpaceX的IPO招股说明书中时，它，它看起来像是绝大部分收入都会来自AI，来自Grok，真的，不会是像SpaceX现在这样把东西运往太空。你的公司在10年后会做什么，又将如何赚钱？

segments.textEn: Well, you can really think of the economy as digital and physical intelligence. So what we have right now advancing very rapidly is digital intelligence. Obviously with AI, that is, it seems that almost with every passing week there are more AI breakthroughs. It can do something amazing that it couldn't do before, but it's still somewhat confined to the digital realm. It doesn't have end effectors. You need the end effectors in the form of humanoid robotics. You need basically lots of bots. In a nutshell, you need lots of bots. And then you can go from intelligence manifesting itself only digitally to shaping atoms. And you say, what is an economy? An economy is the production of goods and provision of services. And if you have vast numbers of robots with vast amounts of digital intelligence, you have a sort of a quasi infinite economy. So this is really. The future is going to be very, very different from the past. There's no analogy or metaphor that I think illustrates the magnitude of change that we're going to experience here.
segments.textZh: 嗯，你完全可以把经济看作数字智能和物理智能。所以，我们现在拥有的、正在非常迅速发展的，是数字智能。显然，随着 AI 的发展，似乎几乎每过一周都会有更多 AI 突破。它能做到一些以前做不到的惊人之事，但它仍然在某种程度上局限于数字领域。它没有末端执行器。你需要以人形机器人的形式存在的末端执行器。你基本上需要大量机器人。简而言之，你需要大量机器人。然后，你就可以从仅以数字形式展现自身的智能，转向塑造原子。你会问，什么是经济？经济就是商品的生产和服务的提供。而如果你拥有数量庞大的机器人和海量数字智能，你就拥有了一种近乎无限的经济。所以这真的。未来将与过去非常、非常不同。我想不出任何类比或隐喻能够说明我们将在这里经历的变化有多么巨大。

segments.textEn: I understand that and I'm also trying to kind of figure out what that world will look like. But in some way you have good.
segments.textZh: 我明白这一点，我也在试图弄清楚那个世界会是什么样子。但从某种意义上说，你有好的。

segments.textEn: It's going to be pretty incredible.
segments.textZh: 那会非常不可思议。

segments.textEn: Yeah, we'll also do. There are some risks, we'll come to those. But just on how then you make money, because in the end people are buying your shares because they expect you to make money.
segments.textZh: 是的，我们也会做。确实存在一些风险，我们会谈到那些。但就你之后要如何赚钱这个问题而言，因为归根结底，人们购买你的股票，是因为他们期望你赚钱。

segments.textEn: I'll make another prediction. Money won't matter in 2036.
segments.textZh: 我再做一个预测。到 2036 年，钱将不再重要。

segments.textEn: I'm not sure that the people who bought your shares think that money won't matter in 2036.
segments.textZh: 我不确定那些购买了你公司股票的人是否认为，到 2036 年钱将不再重要。

segments.textEn: What do you want money for? You want money for goods and services, right? You want money for obviously food, housing, transport, entertainment. Well, if that is so abundant that there's more, that the robots and AI are providing more goods and services than any human could possibly consume, what do you need money for in that case?
segments.textZh: 你要钱做什么？你要钱来购买商品和服务，对吧？显然，你要钱来购买食物、住房、交通和娱乐。好吧，如果这一切都丰富到有更多，多到机器人和 AI 提供的商品与服务超过任何人所能消费的量，那么在这种情况下，你还需要钱做什么？

segments.textEn: But you're creating these robots between now
segments.textZh: 但你从现在起正在制造这些机器人

segments.textEn: and then you'll need money. Sure.
segments.textZh: 而且那时你会需要钱。当然。

segments.textEn: Are you selling these robots? Are you selling humanoid robots? Or are you producing goods and services with the humanoid robots that you control? I give you the Levi straps.
segments.textZh: 你会出售这些机器人吗？你会出售人形机器人吗？还是会用你控制的人形机器人来生产商品和提供服务？我把李维的带子给你。

segments.textEn: I think I would probably be. It would be an exercise in vanity for me to think that I would be controlling super genius AI that is vastly smarter than me. I think what we can and should try to do is to make sure that the AI has good values, that it cares about humanity and that it wants us to be happy and prosper. I think it probably will be. What my biological neural net tells me is that the most important thing for AI safety is to be maximally truth seeking and curious. If that's the case, I think it will foster humanity.
segments.textZh: 我想我可能会是。要是我认为自己能控制远比我聪明的超级天才 AI，那就是一种虚荣之举。我认为，我们能够而且应该努力做的，是确保 AI 拥有良好的价值观，确保它关心人类，并希望我们幸福、繁荣。我认为它很可能会这样。我的生物神经网络告诉我，对 AI 安全而言，最重要的是最大限度地追求真相和保持好奇。如果是这样，我认为它会促进人类发展。

segments.textEn: So let's unpack that. You're sure that humans will no longer be in control in 10 years time?
segments.textZh: 那么，我们来详细分析一下。你确信 10 年后人类将不再掌握控制权吗？

segments.textEn: I think it is unlikely. In the same way that if the difference InTELLIGENCE between AI and humans is vastly greater than the difference in intelligence between AI and chimpanzees, it's hard to imagine that the chimpanzees would be in charge.
segments.textZh: 我认为不太可能。就像如果 AI 与人类之间的智力差距，远远大于 AI 与黑猩猩之间的智力差距，那么很难想象黑猩猩会掌权。

segments.textEn: I'm really satisfied by this.
segments.textZh: 我对此真的很满意。

segments.textEn: And we are essentially an evolved form of chimpanzee. So it wasn't that long ago that we're swinging through the trees and eating bananas in the jungle. And we still eat bananas, by the way. We do. And still, you know, bananas sometimes swing
segments.textZh: 而我们本质上是黑猩猩的一种进化形态。所以就在不久以前，我们还在树林间荡来荡去，在丛林里吃香蕉。顺便说一句，我们现在仍然吃香蕉。确实。而且仍然，你知道，香蕉有时也会荡

segments.textEn: through trees as well.
segments.textZh: 过树林。

segments.textEn: Yes, sometimes Swing through trees is kind of fun. It's sort of reminiscent of the past. For all time's sake, swing through the trees once in a while, probably, you know, there should be more swinging through trees. I bet. It's way more fun than people think.
segments.textZh: 是的，有时在树林间荡来荡去还挺有趣的。这有点让人回想起过去。看在往日时光的份上，偶尔在树林间荡一荡，大概，你知道，应该有更多人在树林间荡来荡去。我敢说。这比人们想象的有趣多了。

segments.textEn: I'm with you on that. I'm definitely with you on swinging through trees. I love swinging through trees. But, but, but I'm really struck listening to you say this now because I've been listening to a bunch of things that you've said over the years. And, and 10 years ago you were on a podcast, I think it was, with Neil Degrasse Tyson, and you said that the thing that terrified you most was rapid recursive self improvement in AIs.
segments.textZh: 这点我同意你。我绝对同意你说的在树林间荡来荡去。我喜欢在树林间荡来荡去。但是，但是，但是现在听你这么说，我真的很震惊，因为这些年来我听过你说的很多东西。而且，而且 10 年前，你上过一期播客，我想是和尼尔·德格拉斯·泰森一起，你说最令你恐惧的是 AI 快速的递归式自我改进。

segments.textEn: Yes.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: And that you said, and it really struck with me. You said that we will just be the pet Labradors at the best. Well now you see, Labrador is pretty happy creatures, but in 2023, you, you caught, you asked for a slowdown in air because you were worried about it.
segments.textZh: 而且你说过，这让我印象非常深刻。你说，最好的情况下，我们也只会成为宠物拉布拉多犬。好吧，现在你看，拉布拉多犬是相当快乐的生物，但在 2023 年，你，你抓住了，你要求放缓空气，因为你对此感到担忧。

segments.textEn: Well, I signed on to, you know, one as one of many, like 500 people. I, I, I, I was just, you know, one of many sign signatures on that thing.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我签署了，你知道，作为许多人之一，像 500 人之一。我，我，我，我只是，你知道，那份东西上众多签名中的一个。

segments.textEn: But, but I think even last year you said, I, what was it? Ted Cruz's podcast, you said there was a 10 to 20% chance of killer robots wiping out humanity.
segments.textZh: 但是，但是我想，甚至就在去年，你还说过，我，是什么来着？在特德·克鲁兹的播客上，你说杀手机器人消灭人类的概率是 10% 到 20%。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: So you sounded worried then. Now you seem very relaxed about it. Have you changed your view?
segments.textZh: 所以你当时听起来很担忧。现在你似乎对此非常放松。你的看法改变了吗？

segments.textEn: I still think there's, I still think there's risk associated with AI and robots. It's not zero. I guess I've come to my sort of philosophical conclusion is to look on the bright side. I can't see any way to really stop this incredible momentum of AI and robots. And at times I sort of think, well, perhaps even if there was a stop button, we probably shouldn't Press it because. Because the most likely outcome is incredible abundance for. For all.
segments.textZh: 我仍然认为存在，我仍然认为 AI 和机器人伴随着风险。风险并非为零。我想，我得出的某种哲学结论是，要看到光明的一面。我看不出有什么办法能真正阻止 AI 和机器人的这种惊人势头。有时我会想，嗯，也许即使有一个停止按钮，我们可能也不该按下它，因为。因为最可能的结果是难以置信的富足，供。供所有人享有。

segments.textEn: That's what I thought. Actually, it struck me that now you seem to have decided it's inevitable. Let's hope for the best and go for the ride.
segments.textZh: 我也是这么想的。实际上，我突然觉得，你现在似乎已经认定这是不可避免的了。让我们抱最好的希望，享受这段旅程吧。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I mean, yes, pretty much. Let's enjoy the ride. I think my philosophy at this point, because I mean, honestly, there seems to be just an inexorable progress here in AI and in robots that even if I wanted to stop it, I couldn't.
segments.textZh: 对，我是说，是的，差不多就是这样。让我们享受这段旅程吧。我认为这就是我目前的哲学，因为，我是说，老实说，AI 和机器人领域似乎正呈现一种不可阻挡的进步，即便我想阻止它，也做不到。

segments.textEn: Do you think there's still a 10 to 20% chance that killer robots mean the end of humanity? That's a high p. Doom, as they say.
segments.textZh: 你仍然认为杀手机器人有 10% 到 20% 的概率会导致人类终结吗？正如人们所说，这是很高的毁灭概率。

segments.textEn: Well, in the long run we're all dead, of course, you know, so I mean, I mean according to the standard model of physics, the end of the universe is a long, boring, sort of thin gray soup of gradual cooling, meaning that sort of the heat death, the universe is called. So if the heat death of the universe is in fact the outcome for our reality, then it really is all about the journey because the destination is terrible.
segments.textZh: 嗯，从长远来看，我们当然都会死，你知道，所以我是说，我是说，按照物理学的标准模型，宇宙的终点是一锅漫长、乏味、逐渐冷却的稀薄灰汤，也就是所谓的热寂，宇宙是这么称呼的。所以，如果宇宙热寂事实上就是我们这个现实的结局，那么真正重要的就全在旅程本身，因为目的地糟透了。

segments.textEn: 10 years is not very. Yeah, I get that. But that could be a long way, very long way. If it's 10 to 20% in 10 years, would you go into one of your rockets if you thought there was a 10 to 20% chance of it blowing up and killing you?
segments.textZh: 10 年并不是很。对，我明白。但那可能还很遥远，非常遥远。如果 10 年内发生这种事的概率是 10% 到 20%，而你认为你的某枚火箭有 10% 到 20% 的概率会爆炸并炸死你，你还会登上它吗？

segments.textEn: Yes, but let's say you can't do anything about it. I guess the only thing we can try to do is minimize the probability of the bad outcome. But trying to stop the intelligence in robots, I mean, for the longest time
segments.textZh: 是的，但假设你对此无能为力。我想，我们唯一能尝试做的，就是尽量降低坏结果发生的概率。但是试图阻止机器人拥有智能，我是说，在很长一段时间里

segments.textEn: I
segments.textZh: 我

segments.textEn: declined to participate in AI or was created OpenAI as essentially a counterweight to Google because at the time they had more or less a monopoly on AI. And then anthropic spun out of OpenAI and if anything it seems like my actions have really accelerated AI. You know, I wasn't really aiming to accelerate AI, but in creating OpenAI and then having anthropic spin out of that, and now currently anthropic's leader in AI. I mean these actions have actually resulted in knock on effects that accelerated AI, which wasn't really my intention. So it just seems like all roads lead to acceleration of AI. So then I'm like, okay, well you can just sort of be sad about it or join the club, I suppose.
segments.textZh: 拒绝参与AI，或者说创建OpenAI，本质上是为了制衡谷歌，因为当时他们差不多垄断了AI。然后Anthropic从OpenAI分拆出来，而真要说起来，似乎我的行动确实加速了AI。你知道，我原本并不是想加速AI，但由于创建了OpenAI，接着Anthropic又从中分拆出来，而现在Anthropic目前是AI领域的领导者。我的意思是，这些行动实际上产生了连锁效应，加速了AI，而这并非我的本意。所以看起来，所有道路都通向AI加速。于是我就想，好吧，你可以只是为此感到难过，或者加入这个俱乐部，我想。

segments.textEn: Well, you've certainly joined the club. Yeah, you've definitely joined the club, but
segments.textZh: 嗯，你显然已经加入这个俱乐部了。是的，你绝对已经加入这个俱乐部了，但是

segments.textEn: you can't beat them, join them, you know.
segments.textZh: 打不过他们，就加入他们，你知道。

segments.textEn: Well, you've clearly done that and very successfully. But what about trying to minimize the risks and you know, a number of the other leaders of model makers have been pushing for different ways to try and minimize the risks. Just last week, Demis Hassabes came out with a proposal for a private public regulator. I think you said it was a good starting point for discussions. I think. Do you think you guys should be working more actively to get something in place to control the risks, or do you think that's impossible, too?
segments.textZh: 嗯，你显然已经这么做了，而且非常成功。但努力把风险降到最低呢？你知道，其他一些模型开发商的领导者一直在推动以不同方式设法把风险降到最低。就在上周，Demis Hassabes提出了一项关于公私联合监管机构的方案。我想你说过，这是展开讨论的一个好起点。我想。你认为你们应该更积极地努力建立某种机制来控制风险，还是你认为那也是不可能的？

segments.textEn: My recommendation to Demis, because I talked to him for a few hours before he published his piece, was that the most immediate thing that we could do is to have the leading AI companies at least just meet or have some sort of call once every few weeks and just discuss any safety and security issues. And that before a breakthrough, sort of a new frontier model is released, something that sort of is far more intelligent than anything that already exists, that there's an opportunity for the various competing AI companies to test that model for any harmful effects and to be able to recommend pausing to address some of these security issues. I think that's. That's the. That's sort of the easy, quick thing that we can do. And it can. It can evolve to more than that over time, but that's. That, I think, would be a smart move.
segments.textZh: 我给Demis的建议是，因为他发表那篇文章之前，我和他谈了几个小时，我们眼下最可以做的事，是让领先的AI公司至少每隔几周见一次面，或者进行某种通话，讨论任何安全和安保问题。而且在一项突破成果，也就是某种新的前沿模型发布之前，如果它远比现有的任何东西都更智能，就让各家相互竞争的AI公司有机会测试该模型是否存在任何有害影响，并且能够建议暂停发布，以解决其中一些安全问题。我认为那是。那是。那算是我们可以做的简单、快捷的事情。而且它可以。随着时间推移，它可以发展成更多东西，但那是。那，我认为，会是明智之举。

segments.textZh: 我们能谈谈人们担心的另一个风险吗，尤其是，我认为，普通美国人所担心的风险，你知道，人工智能已经变得极其不受欢迎。75%的人对此感到担忧，我认为他们担心的是自己的工作。而且如果你看看，Dario曾有一句名言，怎么说来着，50%的入门级工作，入门级白领工作将在几年内消失。你正在制造人形机器人。

segments.textEn: Yes. You also said, like, I mean, Dario did dig his own grave here regarding Mythos, because he said, you know, Mythos is like super scary, terrifying. And also, by the way, we're going to release it. And then he's like, what do you mean? You know, So I think he. I think probably in the future we'll choose its words differently.
segments.textZh: 是的。你也说过，比如，我的意思是，Dario在Mythos这件事上确实是自掘坟墓，因为他说，你知道，Mythos超级吓人、令人恐惧。另外，顺便说一下，我们还要发布它。然后他又像是在说，你什么意思？你知道，所以我认为他。我认为将来大概会换一种措辞。

segments.textEn: But what's.
segments.textZh: 但什么是。

segments.textEn: Because obviously if you terrify everyone and then say, oh, we're releasing this terrifying thing, people will obviously be alarmed about that. You've literally told them to be scared and then you release the scary thing. And so they will be scared. That is natural.
segments.textZh: 因为很明显，如果你把所有人都吓坏了，然后说，哦，我们要发布这个可怕的东西，人们显然会对此感到惊恐。你实际上已经告诉他们要害怕，然后又发布了这个吓人的东西。所以他们会害怕。这很自然。

segments.textEn: So I certainly don't want you to alarm people. But I do think there is a really important debate about how quickly and to what degree AIs displace people from jobs. Because it is, as you say, if within 10 years, it's more. It's. There's more intelligence, artificial intelligence, than any human intelligence.
segments.textZh: 所以我当然不希望你惊吓人们。但我确实认为，关于人工智能将以多快的速度、在多大程度上取代人们的工作，有一场非常重要的辩论。因为这正如你所说，如果在10年内，它更多。它。人工智能的智能超过了任何人类智能。

segments.textEn: Yes.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: And if you are, and I think you're ahead of everyone, at least in this country, on powering humanoid robots, that's. That's also going to be kind of factory work. So do you. Are you part. Do you. Are you closer to Dario, let's say, in your sense of the pace at which jobs are going to be displaced?
segments.textZh: 而且如果你正在，我认为至少在这个国家，你在驱动人形机器人方面领先于所有人，那。那也将会是一种工厂工作。所以你是否。你是其中一部分。你是否。比方说，就你对工作将以何种速度被取代的判断而言，你是否更接近Dario？

segments.textEn: I do think it's going to be a bumpy road because AI will be able to do any job better than any person can do that job. And that will be true very quickly of jobs that are digital or really anything that involves a person at a computer or on a phone. AI could do all of that. We'll be able to do all of that very soon. For software engineering, we already have a situation where AI is better than at least 90% of humans at writing software, 90% of professional software engineers at writing software. And it really is getting to the point where it'll be better than 99%, and then it'll get to the point where there's just no way to compete, it'll. It'll get to what I call Stockfish level. So Stockfish. So Stockfish is the chess program that. Stockfish is so good at chess that you know it, it will easily beat Magnus Carlsen or anyone at chess on a. Even running on a small computer. I suspect that you could probably run Stockfish on your phone and beat Magnus Carlsen. That's how good it is at chess and that's how good AI will be at writing software and beyond.
segments.textZh: 我确实认为这将是一条崎岖的道路，因为人工智能将能够把任何工作都做得比任何能做那项工作的人更好。对于数字化工作，或者其实任何涉及人在电脑或手机上操作的工作，这很快就会成为现实。人工智能可以完成所有这些。我们很快就能完成所有这些。在软件工程方面，我们已经处于这样一种情况：人工智能编写软件的能力胜过至少90%的人类，胜过90%的专业软件工程师。而且现在真的快要到它将胜过99%的程度了，然后它将达到根本无法与之竞争的程度，它会。它会达到我所说的Stockfish水平。所以Stockfish。Stockfish是那个国际象棋程序。Stockfish的棋艺好到，你知道，它能轻松击败Magnus Carlsen或任何棋手，在一台。甚至是在一台小型电脑上运行。我猜，你或许可以在手机上运行Stockfish并击败Magnus Carlsen。它的棋艺就是这么好，而人工智能编写软件以及其他方面的能力也会这么好。

segments.textEn: Software beyond.
segments.textZh: 软件之外。

segments.textEn: And that applies to everything.
segments.textZh: 而这适用于一切。

segments.textEn: Everything, Everything, everything, everything. But what about for physical jobs, for assembly jobs? You will also need the capability in humanoid robots, which so far isn't the there yet, is it?
segments.textZh: 一切，一切，一切，一切。但体力工作、装配工作呢？你还需要人形机器人具备相应能力，而到目前为止还没有达到，对吧？

segments.textEn: Right. So that's why I said digital AI and then physically manifested AI in the form of robots, where the robot is more or less an end effector. It would have some amount of local intelligence, but be managed by a large AI model. And I've said many times, I think work is going to be optional. So I mean, let me. So, so I think maybe, maybe a good, a good comparison would be gardening. Like, you don't have to garden, you know, you don't. Like, you don't have to grow vegetables in your garden. You can go to the store and they're going to be pristine vegetables. Or you could grow vegetables in your garden and there will actually be less perfect. Your tomatoes are not going to be as plump and juicy as the ones at the store. They'll, you know, look a little artisanal. But, you know, if you go to a friend's house and they, they make dinner with vegetables from their garden, it's, It's a nice touch.
segments.textZh: 对。所以这就是为什么我先说数字人工智能，然后再说以机器人形式具象化的人工智能，其中机器人或多或少是一个末端执行器。它会具备一定程度的本地智能，但由一个大型人工智能模型管理。而且我说过很多次，我认为工作将成为可选项。所以我的意思是，让我。所以，所以我认为也许，也许一个不错的、不错的类比是园艺。比如，你不必做园艺，你知道，你不必。比如，你不必在自己的花园里种蔬菜。你可以去商店，那里会有品相完美的蔬菜。或者你可以在自己的花园里种蔬菜，而它们实际上会没那么完美。你的西红柿不会像商店里的那样饱满多汁。它们会，你知道，看起来有点手工制作的感觉。但是，你知道，如果你去朋友家，他们，他们用自家花园里的蔬菜做晚餐，这，这是一份贴心之举。

segments.textEn: So that's what I'm saying.
segments.textZh: 所以这就是我所说的。

segments.textEn: This is what work is going to be like.
segments.textZh: 未来的工作就是这样。

segments.textEn: I get that. I mean, in that world I would be hopeless because I can't garden, save my life. But I get the idea people still like playing chess with each other, even though every computer is better. But let's just, let's just think about the politics of this.
segments.textZh: 我明白。我是说，在那个世界里我会无可救药，因为我怎么也学不会园艺。但我明白这个意思，即使每台电脑都更厉害，人们仍然喜欢彼此下棋。但我们还是，就让我们思考一下这件事的政治问题。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: Because it sounds. You're describing a world where within 10 years, pretty much every job can be done better by an intelligence. And yes, you're seeing huge returns to this intelligence. Two people like you, you're the wealthiest man in the world. What people who lose their jobs, who are displaced, who may go off and garden. But how are they going to live? And what kind of. I mean, it sounds to me it's
segments.textZh: 因为这听起来。你描述的是这样一个世界：在10年内，几乎每一项工作都能由一种智能做得更好。而且是的，你正看到这种智能带来巨额回报。两个像你这样的人，你是世界上最富有的人。那些失去工作、被取代、可能离开去做园艺的人怎么办。但他们要怎么生活？以及什么样的。我是说，在我听来它

segments.textEn: going to be universal, high income.
segments.textZh: 将会是全民高收入。

segments.textEn: But how are you going to get there? Let's talk about the politics of this because right now if we look at the political pressures in most countries, people are very, very worried about this. Very against. Seems to me that there's a risk that we are heading more for revolution than for an easy route to this nirvana you're playing out.
segments.textZh: 但你要怎样实现这一点？让我们谈谈这件事的政治问题，因为现在，如果我们看看大多数国家的政治压力，人们对此非常、非常担忧。非常反对。在我看来，我们面临的风险是，与其说我们正轻松地走向你所描绘的这个极乐世界，不如说我们更可能正走向革命。

segments.textEn: I mean it will be a bumpy road. I'm not suggesting it will be sort of that everything will be smooth sailing here. So I mean there are many jobs that used to exist that don't exist because of computers. I mean the word computer used to refer to a person doing computations like that used to be a job description of a person. And you can see pictures online of buildings that have entire skyscrapers just filled with people doing calculations to do things like calculate the interest on your bank balance. This is how things were done for a long time until computers came around. And even in the beginning computers were very expensive and hard to use. So the thing that's different here is that the pace of change is radically accelerated. But still some people were upset that they the job of calculating bank interest would no longer be available. But now I think you'd be hard pressed to find people who want to do that job. So I think I have a suggestion for say what say science fiction books people might want to read to get a sense of what the future will be like. And the best envisioning of an AI future that I've read are the books by Ian Banks, the culture books.
segments.textZh: 我是说，这条路会很颠簸。我不是说这里的一切都会一帆风顺。所以，我是说，过去存在的许多工作已经因为计算机而不复存在了。我是说，computer（计算员）这个词过去指的是进行计算的人，那曾经是对一个人的职位描述。你可以在网上看到一些建筑物的照片，整栋摩天大楼里全是进行计算的人，做的事情包括计算你银行余额的利息。在计算机出现之前，很长一段时间里事情就是这样完成的。即使在早期，计算机也非常昂贵且难以使用。所以这里不同的是，变化的速度从根本上加快了。但仍然有些人因为计算银行利息这份工作将不复存在而感到不满。但现在，我想你很难找到愿意做那份工作的人。所以，对于人们可以读哪些科幻小说来了解未来会是什么样子，我想我有一个建议。在我读过的作品中，对人工智能未来最出色的构想来自伊恩·班克斯的书，也就是“文化”系列小说。

segments.textEn: I'm just reading Accession so thanks to you I've started reading these. But I actually don't find that future a terribly appealing one because I don't think humans have agency in that future.
segments.textZh: 我刚在读《Accession》，所以多亏了你，我开始读这些书了。但实际上，我并不觉得那种未来特别有吸引力，因为我认为人类在那个未来没有自主权。

segments.textEn: They have agency minimum compared to the mind small way.
segments.textZh: 与心智的小方式相比，他们拥有最低限度的自主权。

segments.textEn: But the irony in Banks as you know was a socialist, Ian Banks had a very different political philosophy.
segments.textZh: 但讽刺的是，正如你所知，班克斯是一名社会主义者，伊恩·班克斯有着非常不同的政治理念。

segments.textEn: I not sure that's. I'm not sure I would entirely agree with that.
segments.textZh: 我不确定那是。我不确定我会完全同意这一点。

segments.textEn: Let's agree that that could be where we end up. I'm concerned about the road and we live, you know, we live in democracies and people are very worried about this. So I guess two questions. Firstly, do you have to have massive redistribution from people like you to the people who are losing their jobs? Do you need to have, do you need to pay more tax? Do you have much higher taxes on capital so that you fund some kind of universal income? Otherwise what do people live off?
segments.textZh: 我们姑且同意，那里可能就是我们的最终归宿。我担心的是这条路，而我们生活在，你知道，我们生活在民主国家，人们对此非常担忧。所以我想有两个问题。首先，你是否必须把财富从像你这样的人大规模再分配给那些正在失去工作的人？你是否需要，你是否需要缴纳更多税款？你是否必须大幅提高资本税，从而为某种全民收入提供资金？否则人们靠什么生活？

segments.textEn: I think that the treasury should just simply issue people checks.
segments.textZh: 我认为财政部应该直接给人们发支票。

segments.textEn: But where's the revenue coming from? I mean I'm enough of an economist if you just issue checks, you're Going to have inflation.
segments.textZh: 但收入从哪里来？我的经济学知识至少足以让我知道，如果你只是发支票，就会引发通货膨胀。

segments.textEn: This is like a lot of what we're trying to think about is these things were relevant in the past, they will not be relevant in the future. So, like, inflation is simply the ratio of money to goods and services. So if the goods and services output increases dramatically, if it increases 1000%, you can increase the. You can literally print or these guys change the database. Never print money. You create money in the database, provided the creation of that money is less than the rate at which goods and services increase. You actually have deflation. So I'll make a prediction, which is that deflation will be the issue, not inflation, because as the output of goods and services increases, if the output of goods and services increases faster than the money supply, you will have deflation.
segments.textZh: 这就像，我们正在努力思考的很多事情是，这些东西过去有意义，但未来将不再有意义。所以，比如说，通货膨胀只是货币与商品和服务之间的比率。因此，如果商品和服务的产出大幅增加，如果增长1000%，你就可以增加。你真的可以印钞，或者这些人修改数据库。从来不印钱。你在数据库里创造货币，只要创造货币的速度低于商品和服务增长的速度。实际上就会出现通货紧缩。所以我要作出一个预测，那就是问题将是通货紧缩，而不是通货膨胀，因为随着商品和服务产出的增加，如果商品和服务产出的增长速度超过货币供应量，你就会出现通货紧缩。

segments.textEn: I'm actually, I'm perfectly willing to believe that you may well be right. Absolutely, you may well be right. But I'm really hung up on how we get from the current polarized, angry, fearful policy we have now to this nirvana. And I think you can paint a picture where people are so scared by this, you know, they essentially try to stop it. Maybe they can't. But you get nationalized. There's a kind of, you know, far left government, there's exorbitant tax increases. The kind of economy crumbles because people are so worried about a future. Which does sound quite scary as you describe it. How do you, how do you handle the politics now?
segments.textZh: 实际上，我完全愿意相信你很可能是对的。绝对如此，你很可能是对的。但我真正纠结的是，我们如何从目前这种两极分化、愤怒、恐惧的政策走向这个极乐世界。我认为，你可以描绘这样一种情景：人们对此恐惧至极，你知道，他们实际上会试图阻止它。也许他们阻止不了。但你会被国有化。会出现某种，你知道，极左政府，税收过度上涨。整个经济会崩溃，因为人们对未来太过担忧。而按照你的描述，这个未来听起来确实相当可怕。你要如何，你现在要如何应对政治问题？

segments.textEn: It's exhilarating and terrifying.
segments.textZh: 这既令人振奋，又令人恐惧。

segments.textEn: But if you were in the. Yeah, exactly.
segments.textZh: 但如果你身处那个。对，没错。

segments.textEn: Honestly, if you ask me, on any given day, in fact, even intraday, I've gone from exhilaration to terror regarding AI. So I want to be clear. I'm not like, I'm not sort of some, you know, I'm not trying to be sort of candide here and just be some, oh, everything's wonderful, some Panglossian view of the world where everything's, you know, going to be great. No, no, no risk. I'm, I'm saying there is some risk.
segments.textZh: 坦率地说，如果你问我，在任何一天，事实上甚至是在一天之内，我对人工智能的感受都曾从振奋转为恐惧。所以我想说清楚。我并不是，我并不是什么，你知道，我不是想在这里当个憨第德式的人，只会说，哦，一切都很美好，抱着某种潘格洛斯式的世界观，认为一切都会，你知道，变得很棒。没有，没有，没有风险。我是说，确实存在一些风险。

segments.textEn: I think we agree on that. I guess I'm trying to be more sort of, you know, small bore and practical and think about what can be done now to limit those risks. And you gave a very strong argument for what you and your fellow model makers could do. What should.
segments.textZh: 我想我们在这一点上意见一致。我想我是在努力更，你知道，更具体、更务实一些，思考现在能做些什么来限制这些风险。你也非常有力地论述了你和其他模型制造者能做些什么。那应该。

segments.textEn: Government probably would be good for us to coordinate and just highlight issues that we see in each other's models to mitigate downside risk.
segments.textZh: 政府，我们进行协调或许会有好处，只需把我们在彼此模型中发现的问题指出来，以减轻下行风险。

segments.textEn: What should, should the government. Should you be paying more tax to fund more transfer programs?
segments.textZh: 应该做什么，政府是否应该。你是否应该缴纳更多税款，为更多转移支付项目提供资金？

segments.textEn: Well, first of all, I do, I do pay A lot of tax. So in fact I set a record for the most amount of taxes ever paid by a human.
segments.textZh: 嗯，首先，我确实，我确实缴纳了很多税。事实上，我创下了人类有史以来纳税金额最高的纪录。

segments.textEn: It's also because you're the world's richest man.
segments.textZh: 这也是因为你是世界首富。

segments.textEn: Well, even before that. So my guess is that I will pay many trillions in tax and I'm fine with that. So yeah, that's just the way it's going to be. But I don't think in a future where money is relevant, I think taxation also becomes somewhat irrelevant.
segments.textZh: 嗯，甚至在那之前就是如此。所以我猜我会缴纳数万亿税款，我对此没有意见。所以，是的，事情就是会这样。但我认为，在一个货币仍有意义的未来，税收也会变得有些无关紧要。

segments.textEn: And what about giving people a sense that they have a share in the upside?
segments.textZh: 那么，让人们感觉自己能分享其中的收益呢？

segments.textEn: Sure.
segments.textZh: 当然。

segments.textEn: Giving people shares in SpaceX and Tesla. Do you think that's. And there's a lot of talk about this right now?
segments.textZh: 把SpaceX和Tesla的股份分给人们。你认为那是。而且现在有很多人讨论这个问题？

Whereas as a private company we're very limited in the number of shareholders we're allowed to have before going public. So as a public company we can have millions of shareholders. As a private company, we're limited to just a few thousand shareholders.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我让SpaceX上市的原因之一，就是让公众能够参与，因为他们可以拥有SpaceX的一部分。而作为一家私营公司，在上市之前，我们获准拥有的股东数量非常有限。所以，作为一家上市公司，我们可以有数百万名股东。作为一家私营公司，我们只能有几千名股东。

segments.textEn: So do you think there should be distribution of shares like, you know, the Alaska Wealth Fund is there for which could you imagine a world. And some people talk about the Trump accounts being a kind of vehicle for this that you share of your equity goes to ordinary Americans.
segments.textZh: 所以你认为应该分配股份吗，比如，你知道，阿拉斯加财富基金就是为此设立的，你能否想象这样一个世界。而且有些人谈到，特朗普账户可以成为实现这一点的某种载体，让你的部分股权归普通美国人所有。

And then because I spend, I don't know, about 30% of my time in California, thereabouts, I pay another sort of roughly a third of the California state taxes, which is, are now around 15%. So, so I pay about 45 in taxes just so people know this. You know, I don't know. It's quite so roughly half, then when I die there'll be another sort of 45%, roughly half that that will be taxed. So at the end of the day it probably I'll have a quarter of what I, what I, whatever I have. segments.textEn: You're going to get a lot of that.
segments.textZh: 你会遇到很多这种情况。

segments.textZh: 是的。所以我只是需要某种方式，大致这样说：听着，各位，我们将专注于时间跨度为5到10年或更长的投资。这会压低我们的短期收益。但从长远来看，我是说，如果你采取长期视角，而且确实有这样的投资者，我们有许多投资者确实采取长期视角。事实上，我非常喜欢散户投资者。事实上，我发现，总体而言，我们的散户投资者有，有，他们非常有洞察力，而且持有非常长期的观点。但如果其中一部分归结为你所说的，投资组合经理的激励结构是什么？他们为什么会对季度收益施加如此大的压力，这在某种程度上是可以理解的，因为他们的薪酬以及能否获得晋升，取决于其投资组合的表现。而且他们只有几年来作出这些决定，随后就会根据这些决定接受评估，有时评估期仅为1年或更短。因此，由于他们承受着获得即时回报的压力，他们继而也向公司施压，要求获得即时回报。所以，一旦你理解了激励结构，这种行为的自然就会随之而来。

segments.textZh: 这些都是影响重大的地缘政治决定。拥有这种权力让你感觉如何？你可以决定战争的结果。这感觉如何？而且，由你拥有这种权力是正确的吗？

segments.textZh: 我倡导和平已经很久了。我几年前发帖说，这里确实需要对俄罗斯作出一些让步。这并不是说我亲俄。我只是务实，否则人们会死上很多年，却一无所获。而事实恰恰如此。

segments.textZh: 我不知道。我的意思是，乌克兰人正在。乌克兰人现在做得相当不错，你知道，凭借那种不可思议的无人机能力打击俄罗斯境内。而某种普遍共识是，你知道，战争的态势正在转变。但我的重点并不太在于
